note: PoC V2.0 test asset — a public GrabCAD sample, not a real NWA product. Schema v2 (2026-07-27): parts are now keyed by canonical `name#index` (see types/product.ts) because 117 of this assembly's 409 real nodes share a name with another node elsewhere in the file — confirmed directly against the GLB, not assumed. The 5 propeller components below (4 corner + 1 middle) are the ONLY parts in this file with an authored `rig` — Try RPM appears nowhere else, by design. Every hub/prop pairing was verified against real vertex/position data (matching x,z coordinates between each propeller and its hub bracket) before being authored here, not guessed from names alone. Most of the assembly's 409 solids still have no authored entry and will show the raw part-number fallback — real production use needs full authoring by someone familiar with the actual product, per MEMORY.md's resourcing finding. SCHEMA v3 (2026-07-30): adds a `sections` layer above `parts` for hierarchical selection — on the assembly screen a click now selects the aircraft section a solid belongs to, and individual solids stay selectable inside the isolated detail view. `parts` is unchanged apart from two corrected propeller labels; the 5 rigs are untouched, so RPM CONTROL and the whole-assembly spin still read exactly the same 5 definitions. Section membership is AUTHORED, never derived at runtime: it was generated once by cad-pipeline/generate_vtol_sections.mjs from geometry bounding boxes (these solids have identity transforms, so node positions are useless) and is hand-editable from here on. Left/right labels follow +X forward and +Z right — corroborated by two of the four independently authored propeller names, but worth confirming against the real product.

part_356#356.description: The fuselage-centerline propeller, distinct from the 4 corner lift propellers — spins around the fuselage's longitudinal axis rather than vertically. Hub is two solids (part_356, the main hub body, and part_373, a smaller mount/spinner piece); the two blade solids (33-61-20-05, mirrored) spin together as one rigid body around the hub.

pitch.derivedFrom: The ONLY rig on this aircraft whose blades are separate solids, so the only one that can pitch rigidly. Measured by cad-pipeline/analyze_blade_separability.mjs: 2 blades across 2 solids, 1 mesh island each, blade centres exactly 139.0 from the spin axis and 180 degrees apart. The 4 corner props are 2 blades fused into 1 watertight solid with no disconnected island to split on, so they author no pitch block and correctly show no pitch control.
